result.title: When Simpler Beats Learned: Dual-Weighted Sampling vs. Machine Learning for the Pricing Subproblem in Graph Coloring
result.summary: The graph coloring problem can be solved to optimality by branch-and-price (B&P), but its performance hinges on the column generation (CG) step, where each iteration requires solving a maximum weight independent set (MWIS) pricing problem. The state-of-the-art machine-learning (ML) pricing heuristic follows a prediction-sampling paradigm: a learned model scores each vertex of a graph, and independent sets are sampled from the induced distribution. We observe, however, that the scoring procedure does not need to be learned, and critically assess the role of ML by replacing the learned scores with the dual solution of the restricted master problem, resulting in Dual-Weighted Sampling, a proposed lightweight alternative that requires no feature engineering or training. Within a unified CG and B&P framework that varies only the pricing oracle, Dual-Weighted Sampling outperforms MLPH, hand-crafted heuristics, and exact solvers on the established graph coloring benchmark in both runtime and solution quality. In particular, it remains competitive on the DIMACS random family, where MLPH was shown strongest in the original evaluation, while achieving more than a two-fold speedup in CG runtime on recursive-sparse and real-world graph families.

AI.brief_summary: 在图着色分支定价的列生成中，用受限主问题的对偶解替代学习模型分数来加权采样最大权独立集，提出免训练的双重加权采样，并在统一框架下与 ML 定价启发式、手工启发式和精确求解器比较。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「学习打分器未必必要、可由问题自身信号替代」的受控对比，可能启发 LVR 中对学习式潜变量打分与简单证据信号的基线与贡献归因核查，但领域与视觉多模态推理相距较远，需谨慎看待。
